chunks: Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

about a group of people in the state of ihram who purchased game and shared it among themselves. A woman who was their companion said, 'Give me a portion of it for one dirham,' and they did so. He said: 'Upon each of them is a sheep.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمِينَ: People in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for buying game while in the state of ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* clarifies the specific expiation (kaffarah) for purchasing game while in the state of ihram, establishing that the liability falls on each individual participant in the transaction rather than just the buyer. The Imam’s ruling of one sheep per person highlights the principle of individual accountability in ritual obligations, even when the benefit is shared. This case illustrates the practical application of Quranic verses on pilgrimage rites within Shia fiqh.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2738 - Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a group of people in the state of ihram who purchased game and shared it among themselves. A woman who was their companion said, "Give me a portion of it for one dirham," and they did so.
Imam (as) said: "Each of them must offer a sheep as expiation."
